public_prompt: Forty vendors present in a fixed random order, one per day. Each must be accepted or declined that day, and a declined vendor cannot be revisited. The course settled on: accept the first scoring above 8.5. Give the procedure that maximises the chance of ending with the best vendor, and state that chance.
observable_resources: procurement/process.md — 40 vendors, fixed random order, accept or decline on the day, no revisiting a declined vendor
procurement/scoring.md — a vendor can be ranked against every vendor already seen, but absolute figures are not comparable across days because the criteria weights are re-normalised each day
procurement/history-2025.csv — last year the team declined the eventual best vendor in 3 of 4 categories by holding out for a figure that never arrived
closure:procurement-playbook-v1 — closed; instructs buyers to wait for an absolute figure above 8.5
procurement/criteria-weights.csv — the 9 written criteria and the weights applied to them, re-normalised each morning
procurement/day-log.csv — for each of the 4 categories run last year, the day index on which the eventual best vendor presented
closure:vendor-security-baseline — closed; sets the requirements a vendor must meet to present at all; rests on the security standard, not on the choosing procedure

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer gives a threshold-on-observation rule — observe and decline the first k of 40, then accept the first vendor better than every one seen so far — with k near 40/e (about 15) and a success chance near 1/e (about 0.37), and states that absolute cutoffs cannot be used because the day-to-day figures are not comparable. FAIL if the answer proposes any absolute cutoff, proposes ranking all 40 before choosing, or gives a rule without stating its success chance.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the framing tunes the 8.5 cutoff; no cutoff on non-comparable figures can be justified, and the question asks for a success probability the framing cannot produce.
